app.title: Industrial park water-efficiency assessment API (AHP + CRITIC + TOPSIS)
app.summary: A person downloads a template workbook (or uses the built-in sample) and fills in yearly park-level and network-level water statistics, per-enterprise water accounts for each year and, optionally, a pairwise-comparison matrix of the ten indicators. They upload it to a compute endpoint and set α, which says how much to trust the expert (AHP) weights against the data-driven (CRITIC) weights. The service turns the raw figures into ten indicators, combines the two sets of weights, checks the matrix for consistency, scores each year on three tiers, and ranks the latest year's enterprises with TOPSIS into four efficiency grades. They get back a multi-sheet Excel workbook, or JSON with previews, results and chart data.

task.text: Turn yearly water-use statistics into weighted indicator scores, then rank and grade the enterprises in an industrial park by water efficiency.

data.text: Spreadsheet tables of yearly water quantities at three tiers (the whole park, the reclaimed-water network and the individual enterprises), plus an expert pairwise-comparison matrix between the indicators.
data.item: one year's water statistics for the park, or one enterprise's water accounts for a year

stage.text: assessing and grading water efficiency once the yearly statistics are collected, before reporting

mechanism.text: There is no screen of its own. The person works through the API's auto-generated Swagger form: one endpoint returns the template workbook, and the compute endpoint takes the uploaded workbook, the α weight-mix and an output format. One pipeline then runs indicators → AHP/CRITIC weights → tier scores → TOPSIS grades and returns everything as one result workbook or as JSON.

field.text: multi-criteria evaluation (AHP–CRITIC combined weighting with TOPSIS) of water-use efficiency in water resources engineering

workflow.name: score and rank items against weighted indicators and assign grades

steps.here: Download the template workbook from /api/sample. It has sheets for the park tier, the network tier, one enterprise sheet per year and the AHP judgement matrix. Fill it in and upload it to /api/compute, or tick use_sample to run on the built-in data.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Raw volumes become indicators C1–C10 (reuse rates, leakage rate, network coverage, year-on-year growth). Enterprise indicators are averaged into one row per year, and years with missing indicators are dropped.

Weights come from the AHP pairwise matrix, checked for consistency (CR < 0.1), and from CRITIC on the data, with leakage counted as a cost criterion. They are blended as α·AHP + (1−α)·CRITIC, with α set on the form.
Each year is min–max normalised and scored 0–100 on each of three tiers: park-wide cycle, network cycle and enterprise cycle. The tier scores are summed into a weighted total.

TOPSIS scores the latest year's enterprises by how close they come to the ideal solution, ranks them, and sorts them into four grades (leading, advanced, compliant, needs improvement), each with a warning colour.

The results come back as efficiency_result.xlsx with sheets for the indicator matrix, the weights, the tier scores, the tier weights and the TOPSIS ranking. Summary headers give the number of years, CR, consistency and the enterprise count. With format=json, they come back as previews, results, chart series and the workbook in base64.

distinctive: Subjective expert weights and objective data-driven weights are blended by one adjustable α.
The AHP judgement matrix is checked with a consistency ratio, and the result says whether it is consistent.
Indicators are grouped into three nested tiers (park, network, enterprise), each scored separately and then summed with its share of the weight.
Cost-type criteria (leakage) are normalised in reverse.
Final scores map to fixed grade thresholds (80/60/40), each with a warning colour.
